answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network maps all nodes onto an identity atlas where establishing each identity requires cryptographic stake burning. Creating n identities scales costs superlinearly via burned collateral C(n) = k * n^2, turning any stale identity into a valueless relic. By anchoring consensus across this verified orchard of validator nodes, attackers face quadratic economic friction that makes multi-agent spoofing mathematically intractable.
